To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the feeling of presence is a very important usability aspect in teleoperation/teleoperation systems; and (2) the feeling of common presence in human service robot interaction can also be an important usability aspect in HRI.
“The development from teleoperation/teleprescence interfaces to the human robot interface is a step from a remote control to a cognitive human-robot interaction.
the telepresence systems can be enhanced to the extent that they can provide a feeling of presence and the usability aspects of different types of interfaces can be evaluated and compared.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of human robot interfaces that support cognitive human-robot collaboration.
the development and evaluation of the human-robot interfaces.
the development and evaluation of different types of interfaces for teleoperation, telepresence and service robots.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of teleoperated interfaces has reached a certain level of maturity.
there are no major differences in usability aspects between teleoperation and teleoperation interfaces and HRI.
the development of telepresence systems and HRIs has been very similar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
teleoperation and telepresent systems are still the best solution for the control and interaction with robots in the case of a remote operator.
we are moving from telepresence and teleoperation to the human-robot interface (HRI) and from telepresence and remote presence to cognitive presence.
teleoperation is still an important and necessary part of the HRI, especially when the robot is performing a task that is not fully understood or is too complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cognitive HRI is a very promising way to improve human robot interaction and that the cognitive human robot interface is a very good candidate to replace the traditional telepresence interface in teleoperation.
the HRI should be based on a cognitive interface and the operator should be able to switch from direct teleoperation to a dialogue and spatial information interface.
the human operator should always be involved in the decision making and the robot has to be capable of asking for help.
